data.title: India's wheat acreage may see steepest fall in 26 years on water shortage
data.description:
India's wheat acreage is poised for its steepest decline in 26 years as fields parched by the weakest monsoon rains in more than a decade spur farmers ​to switch to competing crops in search of better returns, industry officials told ​Reuters.

The drop in planting, coupled with the risk of lower yields brought by a severe El Niño ‌weather pattern, threatens to curb output in the world's second-largest wheat producer, in turn boosting prices and complicating efforts to damp food inflation.

"Wheat needs to be irrigated at least four to five times, but we don't have enough water even to sow the crop," said farmer Vilas Bhutekar in the Jalna district of the western state of Maharashtra.

 

"So we chose chickpeas instead, as they require less water."

India's main winter-sown crop, wheat usually competes for acreage with rapeseed, chickpeas and corn.

India's June-September monsoon rains were the lowest in more than a decade as the drying effect of the El Niño drove rainfall as much as 41 per cent below average in key wheat-growing states such as Punjab, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.

"Wheat needs more water than other competing ‌crops," said Nitin Gupta, deputy country head at agricultural trader Olam Agri India.

"But water is in short supply in some regions this year, which could mean farmers plant less wheat."

Wheat was planted across 5 million hectares (12 million acres) by Nov. 13, down 15.3 per cent from a year earlier, government data show.

Planting for the 2026/27 season is expected to fall about 6 per cent from last year's record of 33.6 million hectares (83 million acres), an average estimate by 10 industry officials shows.

That would be the steepest decline since 2000/01, taking area under the crop to the lowest ​in four years at 31.58 million hectares (78 million acres).

Crop shift

Wheat acreage is expected to stay largely steady in the key ‌northern states of Haryana and Punjab, which have access to reliable irrigation.

But farmers in other states are likely to shift from wheat to less-thirsty crops such as chickpea and rapeseed, industry officials said.

Prices of these crops ​have risen much ‌more than wheat, prompting farmers to shift acreage away from the grain, said Sandeep Bansal, director of a flour miller ‌based in the northern state of Uttar Pradesh.

"Wheat is usually farmers' first choice, but this year other crops are giving better returns," Bansal said.

The state-run Food Corporation of India buys wheat from farmers at the minimum ‌support ​price, which New ​Delhi raised this year by just 1 per cent to 2,610 rupees per 100 kg, the smallest increase since 2002/03.

"The government typically incentivises wheat planting by raising procurement prices by 5 to 6 per cent annually," said ‌a New Delhi-based trader ​with a global trade house.

"This year's 1 per cent hike is, in fact, discouraging farmers from expanding wheat acreage."

data.title: Nifty Bank hits new high; HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank rally up to 21% in November
data.description:
Nifty Bank index movement

 
Nifty Bank index hit a new high of 63,421.30, gaining nearly 1 per cent on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) in Friday’s intraday deals, surging 2.2 per cent in the past two trading days. The sharp rally in private and public sector banks (PSBs) is seen amid strong buying by foreign portfolio investors (FPIs).  On Wednesday, November 18, 2026, Nifty Bank index surpassed its previous high of 61,764.85 touched on February 3, 2026.
 
Thus far in November, the Nifty Bank index outperformed the market by soaring 16 per cent, as compared to a 11 per cent rally in the Nifty 50. According to the National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL) data, FPIs net bought a record number of shares worth ₹1.15 trillion ($12.21 trillion) in November.
 
 
Share price of Punjab National Bank zoomed 26 per cent, while HDFC Bank’s stock price soared 21 per cent and Bank of Baroda, IDFC First Bank and State Bank of India (SBI) by 20 per cent each, so far in the month of November. IndusInd Bank, Yes Bank, ICICI Bank, Union Bank of India, Canara Bank and Axis Bank were up in the range of 15-18 per cent. ALSO READ | SBI, PNB, 3 other PSBs zoom up to 27% in Nov; here's what tech analysts say
 
Meanwhile, in Friday's intraday deals, IndusInd Bank surged 7 per cent, while HDFC Bank, Axis Bank and Union Bank of India gained 2 per cent each.
 

Brokerages view on Nifty Bank, Financials sector

 
"Bank Nifty has witnessed a strong upward rally and has broken the previous day's high, closing with a bullish candlestick, indicating positive price momentum. However, with RSI entering the overbought zone, traders should exercise caution while initiating fresh long positions at current levels. The broader price structure remains bullish, and further upside is possible. Immediate support is placed at 62,500, followed by positional support at 62,000, while the next resistance levels are anticipated at 63,500 and 63,800,” said Vatsal Bhuva, Technical Analyst at LKP Securities.
 
“Bank Nifty extended its record run and outpaced the Nifty 50, surging 1,024 points to settle at a fresh all-time high of 63,063 on Thursday, November 19. In the process, the index cleared both its previous peak of 62,442 and the psychological 63,000 mark. Momentum remains firmly with the bulls, and the trend is expected to stay positive as long as the index holds above today’s low of around 61,950. On the upside, 63,300 is the next level to watch, followed by 63,500,” technical analyst at Axis Securities said.
 
“The trend-deciding level for the day is 62,692. If Bank Nifty trades above this level, it may rally up to 63,434-63,804-64,546 levels. However, if it trades below 62,692 levels, we may witness profit booking in the market, and the index may correct up to 62,322-61,580-61,210 levels,” the brokerage firm said.
 
It is important to note that the bulk of the foreign institutional investors (FII) flows have gone into financial services, particularly the banking majors. FIIs are now buying the very same stocks they have been selling to raise money for the artificial intelligence (AI) trade, said V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: Nepal PM Balen Shah to visit India on November 22-23 at PM Modi's invite
data.description:
Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will embark on a State visit to India from November 22 to 23 at the invitation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Nepal's Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai announced on Friday.

According to the Foreign Secretary, a 34-member government delegation led by Prime Minister Shah will depart from Kathmandu for New Delhi to undertake the high-level engagement.

During the visit, Prime Minister Shah is scheduled to hold a delegation-level meeting on Monday with his Indian counterpart, Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Following the delegation-level talks, the two Prime Ministers will jointly inaugurate various projects relating to energy, while bilateral instruments covering various aspects of cooperation will be signed and exchanged between the two sides.

 

After the delegation-level talks, Prime Minister Shah and Prime Minister Modi will also address a joint press conference, followed by a luncheon hosted by the Indian Prime Minister in honour of the visiting Nepali leader.

As part of his official itinerary in the national capital, Prime Minister Shah will call on President Droupadi Murmu during the visit.

The Nepali Prime Minister will also pay tributes and lay a wreath at the Mahatma Gandhi memorial at Rajghat, besides attending the Nepal-India Business Forum aimed at strengthening commercial and economic ties between the two countries.

Rooted in centuries-old historical, cultural, and geographical bonds, India-Nepal ties are underpinned by the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship and a 1,751-kilometre open border. Commonly encapsulated by the traditional adage "Roti-Beti ka Rishta", symbolising shared livelihoods and familial connections, the bilateral relationship is now evolving towards pragmatic economic, energy, and digital integration under Nepal's new political leadership.

data.title: CEC appointment law: SC declines separate hearing to recall split verdict
data.description:
The Supreme Court on Friday declined a submission to separately list a plea seeking recall of a split verdict delivered by a two-judge bench on whether challenges to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners (ECs) should be referred to a larger bench.

A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the recall application, as well as any challenge to the reference order, could be considered by the five-judge Constitution bench already constituted to hear the batch of petitions challenging the validity of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.

 

The CJI also said the five-judge bench could consider the recall application even after the retirement of one of the judges who delivered the split verdict.

Bhushan said that the recall application should be listed before the original bench comprising Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma, which delivered the split verdict on September 23.

He pointed out that Justice Sharma was due to retire next week. Bhushan further said that Justice Sharma had a conflict of interest and, therefore, the application seeking recall of the verdict ought to be heard by the same bench.

When the CJI suggested that the reference bench could consider the application, Bhushan said the reference order itself was recalled on the ground of an alleged conflict of interest.

However, the CJI said that the issue could be raised before the five-judge Constitution bench, which has been constituted for final adjudication of the constitutional challenge to the 2023 law.

The development follows a split verdict delivered on September 23 by Justices Datta and Sharma on whether the petitions challenging the 2023 law warranted consideration by a larger bench.

The main objection was the exclusion of the CJI from the panel to select the CEC and ECs. The panel now includes the prime minister, the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha and a cabinet minister.

While Justice Datta was of the view that the challenge could be adjudicated by a two-judge bench, Justice Sharma favoured a reference to a five-judge Constitution bench, considering the significant constitutional questions involved.

data.title: Trading still anchors NSE's business as clearing section gains share
data.description:
NSE went public in September via an offer for sale, marking a significant milestone for the country’s largest stock exchange. Its results for the second quarter of the financial year (Q2 FY27), compared with the same period last year, show that its clearing services business grew faster than its dominant trading business in terms of revenue. Clearing revenue rose 13.74 per cent to ₹464.88 crore, against a 9.34 per cent increase in trading revenue to ₹3,603.99 crore. The “others” segment recorded the fastest growth of 32.54 per cent, taking its revenue to ₹211.95 crore. 
 
Trading’s profit surged 157.25 per cent to ₹2,496.21 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with ₹970.36 crore a year ago. The clearing services segment’s profit increased by just 3.34 per cent to ₹280.09 crore from ₹271.05 crore, while “others” grew 49.50 per cent to ₹117.28 crore. Despite clearing's faster revenue growth, trading continued to generate the bulk of segment profitability, with its result rising much more sharply during the quarter. 
 
Trading’s share of gross segment revenue (total segment revenue excluding revenue from other sources) declined from 85.29 per cent in Q2 FY26 to 84.19 per cent in Q2 FY27, while clearing’s share increased from 10.58 per cent to 10.86 per cent. “Others” also gained ground, with its revenue contribution rising from 4.14 per cent to 4.95 per cent. While trading remains overwhelmingly dominant, the rising contribution of clearing and other services suggests a gradual broadening of NSE’s revenue base.

data.title: US lawmakers introduce bill after Indian origin grandmother's deportation
data.description:
A Sikh grandmother's deportation to India after three decades of stay in the US has prompted four California lawmakers to introduce a bill in the US Congress to protect long-term immigrant residents.

The Protect Our Neighbours Act, introduced by Congressman John Garamendi, draws inspiration from the deportation of Harjit Kaur, a resident of the San Francisco Bay Area, by the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) last year.

The draft legislation has also received support from representatives Lateefah Simon, Zoe Lofgren, and Juan Vargas.

"The Protect Our Neighbours Act would provide people, like Ms. Kaur who worked in my district for decades, with a fair opportunity to move beyond a final order of removal and continue building futures here in the US where they have made their homes and families," Simon said.

 

Garamendi said nearly one year ago, ICE cruelly detained and deported Kaur, a 73-year-old grandmother with no criminal record - who faithfully reported to ICE every six months for more than 13 years. 

ALSO READ: H-1B visa workers' children could get Green Card pathway under this US Bill

Her cruel and unreasonable detention and deportation is just one more example of the thousands of individuals across the country whose lives and families have been upended by President Donald Trump's ICE, Garamendi said.

According to the American Immigration Council, roughly 1.19 million people with removal orders remain in the US, many having spent years building lives, raising families, and working here.

Under President Trump, the Department of Homeland Security and ICE have aggressively pursued individuals with final removal orders, regardless of how long the case had been deferred, putting long-term residents who have routinely complied with check-ins at renewed risk of detention and deportation.

The bill seeks to make final removal orders expire 10 years after issuance.

An immigration judge could renew an expired order at the Homeland Security Secretary's request, but only with clear and convincing evidence of significant reasons for the delay unrelated to administrative or funding problems, and new evidence establishing that renewal served the public interest.

People with expired, unrenewed orders could seek lawful status for which they qualify after at least 10 years' continuous US presence, provided they had no conviction for an offence punishable by more than a year in prison.

Renewal would be barred while that petition was pending. A separate provision would allow discretionary permanent residence for certain people physically present in the US with longstanding orders based on specified immigration grounds.

data.title: NSE shares jump 3% to fresh high; JM Financial sees MSCI entry in March
data.description:
NSE share price: Shares of the National Stock Exchange (NSE) were up for the third straight session on Friday, gaining nearly 3 per cent in intraday trading. The improving Indian stock market sentiment is creating a favourable environment for exchanges as stronger trading activity brightens their earnings outlook.
 
NSE's share price hit a fresh high of 2,251 on the BSE, up 2.8 per cent over its last close of ₹2,188.30. It has gained 26 per cent over its initial public offering (IPO) price of ₹1,785.  
 
This week alone, the stock has gained 13 per cent, which has pushed the market capitalisation (m-cap) of India's largest exchange above the ₹5.5 trillion mark. This has helped NSE pip Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) to emerge as the ninth most-valuable Indian company. Currently, LIC is valued at ₹5.13 trillion. 
ALSO READ: Capital Markets: Derivatives surge on volatility; cash, MF flows stay muted
 
 
Domestic brokerage Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) earlier this month said that NSE is well positioned to benefit from the structural deepening of India’s capital markets, with market capitalization-to-GDP at 131 per cent and demat penetration at just 17 per cent of the population.
 
Further, it noted that rising financial literacy, digital onboarding and participation from younger investors provide a long runway for trading activity growth.
 
NSE has a dominant market position, which provides a strong competitive moat. With favorable CAS modifications from Dec 2026, MOFSL expects derivatives volume recovery, while its scalable technology infrastructure and high trading capacity reinforce its leadership. "Diversification into non-transaction revenues and operating leverage should strengthen earnings visibility, with colocation, data feeds and clearing providing recurring income streams," it said, adding that it expects revenue/EBITDA/PAT to grow at 12 per cent/13 per cent/13 per cent CAGR over FY26–29, with EBITDA margins reaching ~77 per cent.
 

NSE to make MSCI debut in March: JM Financial

Additionally, JM Financial, in a note dated November 19, said NSE remains a highly probable candidate to enter the MSCI India Standard Index, scheduled to be announced in February 2027. Meanwhile, the changes will take effect in March 2027. 
ALSO READ: NSE deploys liquid cooling for AI infra, plans over 80 GPUs this quarter
 
After screening the entire India EQS universe and recent reshuffle against the indicative MSCI thresholds, we identified NSE, listed on September 24, 2026 with around $45 billion market capitalisation at listing, as far above the minimum size requirement and liquidity metrics, said JM Financial analyst Abhishek Kumar. It was not eligible in November 2026 because it was shy of MSCI's three-month minimum trading history at implementation.
 
If included, NSE could witness $1,511 million in passive inflows, as per the brokerage's estimates.
 
MSCI potential inclusions (Feb 2027)
 
Other stocks that have a high possibility of entering the MSCI index are: Ather Energy, Glenmark Pharma, Kalyan Jeweller and UNO Minda.

data.title: EPFO changes PF withdrawal rules: Retirees can now opt for monthly payouts
data.description:
The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has approved a major change in how subscribers can access their retirement savings, allowing retiring members to draw their provident fund (PF) corpus in monthly, quarterly or half-yearly instalments instead of taking the entire amount as a lump sum.
 
The decision, taken at the 240th meeting of the Central Board of Trustees (CBT) on November 19, 2026, introduces a voluntary Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for retiring members. The remaining balance will continue to earn returns within the EPF system, providing retirees with an additional source of periodic income.
 
The board has also reduced the minimum balance that members must retain in their PF accounts from 25% to 10% and cut the waiting period for final PF settlement after unemployment from 12 months to two months.
 
 
The changes could benefit subscribers who need greater access to their savings as well as those who want to preserve their retirement corpus and draw income gradually. 
 
 1. What is the new EPFO systematic withdrawal plan?
 
Until now, members retiring at the prescribed age could withdraw their accumulated EPF balance as a lump sum. Under the new proposal, they will be able to retain their savings within the EPF system and receive periodic payouts.
 
The withdrawal frequency will include:
- Monthly payouts
- Quarterly payouts
- Half-yearly payouts
 
The unwithdrawn balance will continue to earn interest at the prevailing EPF rate. The facility will be voluntary, so members who prefer to withdraw their entire eligible corpus can continue to choose a lump-sum settlement, subject to the applicable rules.
 
The proposal also provides for nominees or dependants to either withdraw the remaining balance or continue receiving periodic payments if the member dies during the payout period.
 
Around 6.32 lakh EPF members aged above 55 years with provident fund accumulations exceeding ₹5 lakh are expected to be the primary beneficiaries during the initial phase, according to the Labour Ministry. 
 
 2. How is an EPF systematic withdrawal different from a lump-sum withdrawal?
 
The key difference is how the retirement corpus is accessed.
 
Under a lump-sum withdrawal, the member receives the eligible accumulated balance at once and must decide how to invest or use it. Under the proposed SWP, the money can remain within the EPF system, with withdrawals made at regular intervals.
 
For example, consider a person retiring with an EPF balance of ₹30 lakh.
 
Lump-sum option:The member withdraws the entire eligible ₹30 lakh and decides where to invest it.
 
Systematic withdrawal option: The member leaves the corpus in EPF and receives periodic payments. The remaining balance continues to earn the prevailing EPF interest, subject to the final scheme provisions.
 
Combined option: The member may be able to take an initial lump sum and receive periodic payouts from the remaining balance.
 
The last two options are intended to reduce the pressure on retirees to reinvest a large amount immediately after retirement. However, the precise payout calculations, withdrawal tenure and operational conditions will depend on the final notified framework.
 
 3. Will the remaining EPF balance continue to earn interest?
 
Yes. The Labour Ministry has said that the unwithdrawn balance will continue to generate returns within the EPF system.
 
This is an important feature because retirees will not have to move their entire retirement savings into another financial product simply to generate periodic income.
 
However, interest will be earned on the remaining balance, not the original corpus after withdrawals have been made. As money is withdrawn, the amount left to earn interest will reduce.
 
 4. What happens to the 25% minimum balance requirement?
 
The EPFO board has reduced the minimum balance requirement from 25% to 10% of the member's contributions.
 
In practical terms, this means members will be required to retain a smaller portion of their eligible PF balance, allowing greater access to accumulated savings under the applicable withdrawal provisions.
 
The change effectively increases the portion that may be accessed from 75% to 90%, subject to the relevant eligibility and withdrawal conditions. 
 “The reduction in the minimum PF balance requirement from 25% to 10% gives employees greater access to their PF savings through partial withdrawals for permitted needs such as housing, medical treatment and education. In practical terms, members can now access up to 90% of their PF balance, compared with 75% earlier, while retaining a smaller portion for long-term social security," said Puneet Gupta, partner at EY India.
  
 5. Can you withdraw your entire PF balance after leaving a job?
 
The waiting period for final EPF settlement after unemployment has been reduced from 12 months to two months.
 
This reverses the change introduced in October 2025, when the waiting period for premature final PF settlement was extended to 12 months.
 
Under the revised decision, members who leave employment and remain unemployed for two months will once again be able to seek final settlement, subject to the applicable conditions.
 
6. Does the new SWP replace the monthly EPS pension?
 
No. The proposed SWP is a facility to draw down the accumulated EPF corpus. It is separate from the monthly pension paid under the Employees' Pension Scheme.
 
Members with at least 10 years of eligible pensionable service can separately qualify for an EPS pension, subject to the scheme's conditions. The EPFO's new withdrawal facility is intended to supplement this pension income rather than replace it.
 
A retiree could therefore have two potential sources of retirement income: the monthly EPS pension, where eligible, and periodic withdrawals from the EPF corpus.
 
7. What are the tax implications of periodic PF withdrawals?
 
The Labour Ministry has said that a corresponding amendment to the Income Tax Act is being taken up with the Ministry of Finance. The tax treatment of periodic withdrawals and interest earned on the balance retained within EPF will therefore need to be examined.
 
Puneet Gupta, partner at EY India, told Business Standard that the proposed plan could give retirees greater flexibility by allowing periodic withdrawals while the remaining corpus continues to earn EPF returns. This could provide regular income and reduce the immediate reinvestment risk.
 
However, Gupta flagged taxation as an important issue, particularly whether instalment withdrawals and interest earned on the remaining balance would receive the same tax treatment as eligible lump-sum withdrawals. 
 
Under the existing tax framework, EPF withdrawals are generally exempt when the prescribed conditions, including the five-year continuous service condition, are met. Early withdrawals can have different tax consequences. 
 
8. When will the new EPFO withdrawal rules come into effect?
 
The CBT has approved the proposals, but members cannot assume that the new facilities are immediately available.
 
The necessary amendments to the EPF Scheme will have to be approved and notified by the Labour Ministry. The SWP proposal will also require a corresponding amendment to the Income Tax Act, which is being taken up with the Finance Ministry.
 
9. What else has EPFO approved?
 
The CBT also approved UAN-linked mechanisms that would allow members to make voluntary contributions independently of conventional employer payroll systems.
 
The proposal includes third-party micro-contributions, such as customer tips, into provident fund accounts. This could eventually widen access to retirement savings for gig workers, platform workers and others who do not have conventional employer-led PF contributions.
 
The board also approved in-principle investments of up to 3% of fresh accretions in eligible Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), within EPFO's existing overall investment ceiling. Initially, these investments will be routed through government-backed entities.
 
Other decisions included amendments to the Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI) Scheme, 2026, to provide eligible establishments a six-month window to renew expired exemptions and relief for verified transitional periods.
 
 What should EPF subscribers do now?
 
For employees approaching retirement, the proposed SWP could offer an alternative to withdrawing the entire PF corpus and deciding where to reinvest it. But the choice between a lump sum and periodic withdrawals should depend on other retirement income, expenses, liquidity requirements and the size of the accumulated corpus.
 
Those who have recently left employment should also note the proposed reduction in the final settlement waiting period, while waiting for the revised scheme to be formally notified.

data.title: SSC JE answer key 2026 released, check steps to download and deadline
data.description:
The Staff Selection Commission (SSC) released the SSC JE Paper 1 Answer Key for 2026 along with candidates' response sheets on November 19, 2026. Individuals who participated in the Junior Engineer (JE) Examination for 2026 can access their provisional answer keys and response sheets from the official site at ssc.gov. in. 
 
Additionally, the commission activated the objection window, permitting candidates to contest the provisional answers within the designated timeframe. The SSC JE Paper 1 examination for the positions of Civil, Electrical, and Mechanical was conducted from November 2 to November 6, 2026. 

SSC JE Answer Key 2026: Important Dates

Examination Dates- November 2 to 6, 2026
 
 
Answer Key Release Date- November 19, 2026
 
Response Sheet Status- Released
 
Objection Window Opens- November 19, 2026, 6:00 PM
 
Last Date to Raise Objections: November 22, 2026, 6:00 PM. 

How to download SSC JE Answer Key 2026?

Visit the official SSC website at ssc.gov.in.
 
Navigate to the Answer Key section or candidate login portal.
 
Search for the notification titled Junior Engineer Examination 2026: Uploading of Tentative Answer Keys along with Candidates' Response Sheets.
 
Click on the answer key link.
 
Enter your Registration Number and Password.
 
Submit the login details to access your response sheet.
 
View the answers marked during the examination against the provisional answer key.
 
Download and save the response sheet for later reference. 
ALSO READ: NTA UGC NET December 2026 schedule out, check subject-wise exam dates

SSC JE Answer Key 2026: How to raise objections?

Individuals who identify wrong answers or discrepancies in the provisional answer key may raise objections via the SSC Challenge Management System. The Commission established a specific timeframe for submitting these representations. Candidates must finish this process within the given timeline. 
 
Participants should thoroughly examine their questions and answers before filing a challenge. A separate fee must be paid for each question or answer contested. The objection window details are given below:
 
Objection Window Opens- November 19, 2026
 
Opening Time- 6:00 PM
 
Last Date- November 22, 2026
 
Closing Time- 6:00 PM
 
Objection Fee- ₹50 per question/answer
 
Submission Mode: Online only. 

Details mentioned on SSC JE Response Sheet 2026

The answer sheet enables participants to review their provided answers and evaluate them against the provisional answer key. The provisional answer key for Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering positions will be published separately after the exam. Participants can look into the subsequent information that is typically included:
 
Questions asked in the examination
 
Options available for each question
 
Answers chosen by the candidates
 
Correct answers given in the tentative answer key. 
ALSO READ: MHT CET 2027 exam dates released, check registration and other details

What happens after the SSC JE Answer Key 2026?

After downloading the preliminary answer key, individuals should compare their answers with the provisional ones and evaluate their estimated results. Those who identify any inconsistencies must raise their concerns by November 22, 2026, at 6:00 PM. 
 
The SSC will examine the submitted objections within the designated deadline before finalizing the answer key.
